name: Text field
summary: Lets people enter or edit a single line of text.
description: A text field collects one line of free text: a name, an email address, a search term, a quantity typed as text. It has a visible label above, an optional description and, when its value fails validation, a message under it. Several lines of text are a Textarea; a choice among known values is a Select.

anatomy.description: Root. Stacks the label, the control, the description and the message; carries the size and the forced state.
Text naming the field. Provides the accessible name; activating it focuses the control.
The editable box: the native single-line text input, drawn by the component. Receives focus, holds the value and shows the placeholder while empty.
Optional help text under the control (format, example, consequence), associated with it as its description.
Text saying what the severity means (what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check, what was confirmed), associated with the control as a description. Shown only with a severity.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Control height, value text and inline padding take the height, the text size and the inline padding of the Button of the same size; the label takes the text size of the value; the description and the message take the helper sizes.

options.description: Dense forms, toolbars, table rows (28 px high).
Prominent, single fields: a search page, a sign-in form (44 px).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What the field asks for, as a noun phrase (Email address). Always visible.

properties.name: Placeholder
properties.description: Short hint shown while the field is empty, in a lighter color. It disappears when people type: never the label, never an instruction people must remember.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text: expected format, example, or what the value is used for.

properties.name: Message
properties.description: What the severity means: what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check, or what was confirmed. Shown with a severity, in the color of that severity, and replaces errorMessage.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: The field must be filled to submit the form.

properties.name: Read-only
properties.description: The value can be read, focused and copied but not edited (a generated identifier).

properties.name: Severity
properties.description: What the check of the value found. Replaces the invalid boolean: error, warning and success are the three severities of a form control (decision forms-severity); information that holds before any check is the description's job.

options.description: No severity: nothing was checked, or there is nothing to say (default).
The value is not accepted: the border takes the error color, the message says what is wrong and how to fix it, and the control is exposed as in error (aria-invalid on the web).
The value is accepted but deserves attention: the border takes the warning color and the message says what to check. No web state: said in the message text.
The value was checked and confirmed: the border takes the success color and the message says what was confirmed. No web state: said in the message text.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Non-interactive and skipped by the keyboard; the value stays visible. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.

states.description: Resting: an outlined box on the default surface.
Pointer over the control. The box takes the surface hover tint; the border does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.

Focus on the control, from the keyboard or a pointer: an editable field shows the focus color as a 2.4 px outline drawn flush over its border however it was focused; the border and the text do not move.
Severity error: an outline in the error color is drawn flush over the border (1.2 px at rest, 2.4 px with focus) and the message is shown under the control, in the error color.

Severity warning: an outline in the warning color is drawn flush over the border (1.2 px at rest, 2.4 px with focus) and the message is shown under the control, in the warning color. No web state beyond the data attribute.

Severity success: an outline in the success color is drawn flush over the border (1.2 px at rest, 2.4 px with focus) and the message is shown under the control, in the success color. No web state beyond the data attribute.
Not editable: the box takes the level 1 surface; the value stays focusable and selectable.
Non-interactive. Box, value, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors; hover and focus do not apply.

notes: Label, control, description and message stack, separated by container.gap; the control fills the width of the component, which the layout sizes.

Inline padding, minimum height and text size come from the size option; the corner radius (2 px at small, 4 px at medium and large, as the Button's) comes from it too; the border width does not change.

name.text: Computed from the label, associated with the control as its label element on the web. The description and the message are exposed as the accessible description, not as part of the name. The placeholder is exposed as a placeholder and used as a name only when nothing else names the control, which never happens here.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the control. A disabled control is not focusable and is skipped.

guidelines.text: Expose the textbox role, the name, the value and the required, read-only, disabled and error states through the platform's native text input, so assistive technology receives them without extra work.
Use the native input type=text (or email, tel, url for those purposes) without a list attribute: it exposes the textbox role, its value and states without ARIA.
Every field has a visible label associated with the control programmatically; help text that people need to fill the field (format, example) is visible too, as the description.
Associate the label with a label element whose for attribute names the control's id; reference the description and the message with aria-describedby, so they are read after the name.
The placeholder is a short hint, never the label and never an instruction: it disappears as soon as people type, and is not exposed as the name when a label exists.
Show a hint in a text field to help communicate its purpose; because placeholder text disappears when people start typing, include a separate label describing the field.
Apple's recommended minimum text size is 11 pt on iOS and iPadOS; the 12 pt text of the description and the message is above it.

Say the severity in text next to the field, whatever it is: the message names what is wrong and how to fix it for an error, what to check for a warning and what was confirmed for a success, and is associated with the control. Color is never the only sign of a severity.

Say that the value is in error with aria-invalid="true" on the control, for the error severity only, and that a field is required with the required attribute, which the browser exposes as required. The web has no state for a warning or a success: the message says them, and aria-invalid is never set for them.
Mark required fields in the label or the description, never by the error color alone.

Label, value, description and message text contrast at least 4.5:1 with their background in every color mode and enabled state: label and value 19.03:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface, description 12.78:1 and 8.86:1, placeholder 6.08:1 and 6.40:1, message text in its severity color: error 6.12:1 and 7.06:1, warning 13.01:1 and 11.17:1, success 7.87:1 and 7.89:1 (on every surface level the lowest are error 5.79:1 in light mode and 5.30:1 in dark mode, warning 12.30:1 and 8.38:1, success 7.44:1 and 5.92:1). Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

The border is what identifies the field, so it contrasts at least 3:1 with the adjacent surface in every color mode: 12.78:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface at rest, 12.09:1 and 10.33:1 on the hover tint; the severity borders and outlines (the accent functional border): error 6.12:1 and 4.97:1, warning 3.27:1 and 8.09:1, success 7.87:1 and 6.08:1 on the default surface, and at least 5.79:1 and 3.73:1 (error), 3.09:1 and 6.07:1 (warning), 7.44:1 and 4.57:1 (success) on every surface level; the focus outline 5.77:1 and 12.76:1. The outlines are drawn over the border, on the surface around the field, so they are checked against it. Disabled is exempt. A warning border on the subtle warning fill, which a field may take as its fill in step 6, is 2.95:1 in light mode: a known shortfall (issue #119).

A visible focus indicator appears when the control receives focus: a 2.4 px outline in the focus color drawn flush over the border, at every size, so focus is visible by pointer and keyboard alike (WCAG 2.4.7). WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA) is not met at 1x and 2x, because the part of the outline over the border changes contrast only 2.21:1 in light and 1.13:1 in dark, and the fields do not claim it.

The focus outline is drawn with :focus-visible, which browsers match whenever an editable field has focus, pointer or keyboard. It is a CSS outline, never a box-shadow, so forced colors mode repaints it in a system color.

The severity outline (1.2 px) and the focus outline (2.4 px) differ by width, so a field with a severity is not mistaken for a focused one, in forced colors too, where both take the same system color. At 1x the severity outline is as wide as the 1 px border at rest: the severity's color and the message say what the severity is, never the color alone.
Every size is a pointer target of at least 24 x 24 CSS pixels through its minimum height: 28, 36 and 44 pixels.

The label, description and message are set from 12 to 16 px, under the large text size of the contrast criterion (18 pt, about 24 px), so their colors keep 4.5:1. WCAG sets no minimum text size: it asks that text resize up to 200 % without loss of content or functionality, which the box allows because its height is a minimum that grows with larger text.

Fields that collect information about the person (name, email, phone, address) carry the matching autocomplete token, so browsers and assistive technology can identify their purpose. The template passes it through its extra attributes.
A read-only field keeps its value focusable and selectable and is exposed as read-only; a disabled field leaves the focus order. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.

Apple recommends a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt; the small and medium sizes (28 and 36 pt) fall under it on iOS today and the large size (44 pt) reaches it: the Figma library has no platform heights.

Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; all three sizes (28, 36 and 44 dp) fall under it on Android today. Expose an error with the error semantics so the message is announced with the field.
Color transitions of the control are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

guidelines: The label is a noun phrase naming the information asked for: Email address, Company name. Sentence case, no colon, no trailing punctuation.
The description gives the format or an example when it is not obvious: We will only use it to send your receipt.
The placeholder, when any, is a short example of a valid value (name@example.com), never an instruction and never the label.
The message of an error says what is wrong and how to fix it: Enter an email address with an @.

props.label: Email address
props.description: We will only use it to send your receipt.

examples.name: Medium, error
examples.description: Validation failed: the message says how to fix it.

props.label: Email address
props.message: Enter an email address with an @.

examples.name: Medium, warning
examples.description: The value is accepted but deserves attention: the message says what to check.

props.label: Email address
props.message: Warning: check the domain, it looks like a typo of example.com.

examples.name: Medium, success
examples.description: The value was checked and confirmed: the message says what was confirmed.

props.label: Workspace identifier
props.description: Generated when the workspace was created.

decisions.text: The fill of the box is the page's own level, not a level above it: at rest global.bg.level.0.default, on hover global.bg.level.0.hover, and when read-only global.bg.level.1.default, the next level, which is how a read-only field differs from an editable one, on every platform. The fill does not identify the field, the border does (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 for a fill that identifies a text input, and no neutral fill reaches 1.5:1 against the surface; the border color is decided separately). The fill is the one every form control reads (Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch). The decision keeps the tokens as they were: no token changes. The Number field, the Search field and the Textarea follow through the mirror check (decision field-family-mirrors). Not decided here: the disabled fill (global.bg.state.disabled.default, translucent). The team may revisit it after the Text field for every component, and every form control reads that one token, so it changes in one place.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep the page level (chosen); B, Figma's level 1 (#F7F7F7 at rest, #EAEAEA on hover: global.bg.level.1.default and .hover, read-only moved to level 0), rejected because on the light level 1 and 3 surfaces the fill equals the surface, so the field would change look by surface, and it would split the field family from the Select, Checkbox, Radio and Switch, which all read level 0; C, the default Button's translucent global.bg.subtle.neutral.default and .hover, rejected because it fails WCAG 1.4.3 in dark: the placeholder on the hover fill measures 4.46, 4.08, 3.83 and 3.49:1 on levels 0 to 3, and 4.33:1 at rest on level 3 (placeholder and text shown on hover are in scope of Understanding 1.4.3). Reasons for A: no neutral fill can identify the field, the best reaches 1.43:1 against the surface, under the 3:1 of Understanding 1.4.11 (Figure 34), so the border identifies it; Material 3 says its filled and outlined text fields provide the same functionality; one fill rule for every form control; a read-only field must stay distinct from an editable one, as the Windows text box guidance warns that a read-only box that looks editable confuses people. Measured on the resolved tokens at rest on level 0: value 19.03:1 light, 11.28:1 dark; placeholder 6.08:1 light, 6.40:1 dark; lowest over levels 0 to 3, placeholder 5.75:1 light, 5.86:1 dark.

decisions.text: A field draws its focus and severity indicators as outlines flush over its border, never as a thicker border: the border stays stroke-width.sm (0.6 px) in every state, so the text never moves. Focus (:focus-visible, which an editable field matches for pointer and keyboard focus alike) is an outline of focus.ring.width (2.4 px) in color.focus.ring; a severity (error, warning or success) at rest is an outline of stroke-width.md (1.2 px) in the severity's border color (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default); a severity with focus is an outline of focus.ring.width in the severity's color, not the focus color. The outline offset is minus the border width, computed in the CSS as calc(-1 * border-width) because a DTCG alias cannot negate a token, so the outline covers the border exactly and the visible line is 2.4 px (focus, a severity with focus) or 1.2 px (a severity at rest), growing outward. There is no separate ring with a gap any more: the four fields no longer read focus.ring.offset, and text-field.control.outline-offset.focus-visible is removed. The Number field, the Search field (focus only: it has no severity) and the Textarea follow through the mirror check (decision field-family-mirrors). The Focus foundation records the exception (decision text-entry-flush, Focus 0.3.0).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among options: A, keep the 0.6 px border and the ring at a gap (today); B, the Figma library's 1.2 px border on focus and invalid; C, 1.2 px on invalid only; D, 1.2 px in every state; E1 and E3, a thicker border (or an inset outline) on focus, rejected because the text moves with the border and a border change is not repainted in forced colors as an outline is; E4, an outline over the border at offset 0 or minus the border width, colored (a) in the error color or (b) in the focus color when invalid. Chosen: E4a at offset minus 0.6 px. The text never moves, outlines are repainted in system colors in forced colors mode (MDN, forced-colors), and there is one focus width, 2.4 px, as the Button's. Material 3 draws the same pattern, a 1 dp outline at rest and a thicker one in primary on focus, and in the error color when invalid, with no color of its own for the focused error. Known consequences: (1) the severity outlines read the accent functional borders (decision forms-severity), which reach 3:1 against every surface level (Color foundation decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1), so they meet WCAG 1.4.11 where the base error border first chosen was 2.80:1 against surface level 3 in dark. (2) At offset minus 0.6 px, WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA, information only) is not met at 1x and 2x: the part of the outline over the border changes contrast only 2.21:1 in light and 1.13:1 in dark, so the qualifying band is the outward 1 to 1.5 px, under the area the criterion asks for; the fields drop the Focus foundation's 2.4.13 claim, and 2.4.7 and 1.4.11 are still met. (3) At 1x, a severity at rest draws a 1 px line, as at rest (the outline covers the 1 px border): the color and the message are the cues, never the color alone (1.4.1). (4) The focus outline in the severity's color of a field with a severity breaks the Focus foundation's single focus color; the foundation records the exception. The severity outline stays distinguishable from the focus one by width (1.2 against 2.4 px), including in forced colors (F78).

decisions.text: A field takes the corner radius of the Button of the same size, the Shape foundation's rule for controls: small 2 px (corner-radius.2xs), medium and large 4 px (corner-radius.xs), on every platform. text-field.control.border-radius becomes one value per size, as the Button's container.border-radius; the radius is the same in every state. The Number field, the Search field and the Textarea follow through the mirror check (decision field-family-mirrors). Changes the single 4 px radius of the Figma-library import (decision sizes); everything else is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep corner-radius.xs (4 px) at every size, which breaks the Shape foundation at small (a small field would be rounder than the small Button next to it); B, the Shape foundation, the same radius as the Button of the same size, chosen; C, Figma's 4 px read as corner-radius.2xs at every size, which would change the Shape foundation, make the Button differ at medium and large, and keep shadcn's shared rounded-md from following. B keeps one rule for every control and puts a field and a button side by side with the same corners.

decisions.text: The parts of a field are 6 px apart: label and box, box and description, description and message, at every size and in every state (text-field.container.gap, space.4 to space.6), on every platform. It is one token, so the box never moves when the state changes: the message, the description and the label are stacked at the same distance whether or not they are shown (Shape foundation, same box rule). The Number field, the Search field and the Textarea follow through the mirror check (decision field-family-mirrors). Changes the 4 px gap that the decision sizes and the Figma-library import state; everything else they state is unchanged. Left for later: the gap between the label and its required mark (Figma 2 / 4 / 4 px) is its own step, and the Checkbox group and Radio group legends (container.row-gap, space.8) follow with the complex controls (#105).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep space.4 (4 px); B, Figma's resting variants (label to box 6 px at every size, box to description to message 4 / 6 / 8 px, two tokens); C, Figma's validation variants (label to box 6 / 8 / 10 px, the rest 4 / 6 / 8 px); D, one step more everywhere, 6 px, chosen. Figma contradicts itself: the label to box distance is 6 px in the resting variants but 6 / 8 / 10 px in the error, warning, success and disabled ones, which would move the box when the state changes, against the Shape foundation's same-box rule. One token at 6 px gives the label and the help text room to breathe without that.

decisions.text: The label scales with the field and the help text is smaller. The label takes the text size of the value and of the Button of the same size: small 14 px, medium 16 px, large 16 px (body.size.sm, md and md), in medium weight, with the tight line height (1.2) of single lines and the normal letter spacing. The description and the message take the helper sizes: small 12 px, medium 12 px, large 14 px (body.size.xs, xs and sm), with the normal line height (1.5) and the normal letter spacing; their weights are unchanged (regular for the description, medium for the message). Each part is a typography token per size (text-field.label.typography.<size>, text-field.description.typography.<size>, text-field.message.typography.<size>), as text-field.control.typography is, on every platform. The Number field, the Search field (which has no message) and the Textarea follow through the mirror check (decision field-family-mirrors). Changes the single 14 px style (and the 1.5 line height of the label) that the decisions sizes and value-text-button-size state for the label, the description and the message; everything else they state is unchanged. Left for later: the Checkbox group and Radio group legends and the Slider label use the same 14 px style today and follow with the complex controls (#105).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep the single 14 px style for the label, the description and the message; B, the label follows the field (14 / 16 / 16 px) and the help text stays 14 px; C, the label follows the field and the help text takes Figma's helper sizes (12 / 12 / 14 px), chosen; D, Figma's sizes (label 12 / 14 / 16 px, help text 12 / 12 / 14 px, compact line height), rejected because the label would be smaller than the value at the small size and the Typography foundation would need an exception. A label above a field reads at the field's own size, and the help text is secondary to what it describes.

decisions.text: The inline padding of the box is the inline padding of the Button without an icon, size for size: small 8 px, medium 12 px, large 16 px (space.8, space.12 and space.16, the semantic tokens button.container.padding-inline reads at the same size), on every platform. A field and a Button of the same size start their text at the same inset. The decision keeps the values the box already had: no token changes. The Number field, the Search field and the Textarea follow through the mirror check (decision field-family-mirrors).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep the inline padding of the Button without an icon (8 / 12 / 16 px), chosen; B, Figma's 6 / 8 / 10 px; C, the Button's label-side padding (8 / 8 / 10 px), rejected here because it belongs to the question of a leading icon in the field. A field and a Button of the same size start their text at the same inset.

decisions.text: The minimum height of the box takes the height of the Button of the same size: small 28 px, medium 36 px, large 44 px (space.28, space.36 and space.44, the semantic tokens button.container.min-height reads at the same size), on every platform. The box keeps its inline padding and has no block padding: the line of text is centred in the height. A field and a Button of the same size are as tall. The Number field, the Search field and the Textarea follow through the mirror check (decision field-family-mirrors). Changes the 32 / 40 / 48 px minimum heights that the decisions sizes and value-text-button-size state; everything else they state is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep 32 / 40 / 48 px (one step taller than the Button of the same size); B, the Button's heights 28 / 36 / 44 px, chosen; C, the height Figma's padding gives with the new text (33.6 / 40 / 44 px), which matches neither the Button nor today's; D, Figma's heights rounded up (36 / 40 / 44 px). A field and a Button of the same size line up (a search field next to its button, a form row), and the large size reaches the 44 pt that Apple recommends. The hit region of the small and medium sizes is a later step, as for the Button.

decisions.text: The value and placeholder text of a field takes the text size of the Button of the same size: small 14 px, medium 16 px, large 16 px (body.size.sm, md and md, the semantic tokens of button.label.typography at the same size), on every platform. The rest of its style is the Typography foundation's single-line style: regular weight, normal letter spacing and the tight line height (1.2); it is not the Button label's own style (medium weight, compact line height, tight letter spacing). The rule is enforced by pnpm validate (scripts/lib/text-size-rules.mjs): text-field.control.typography.<size> and button.label.typography.<size> must alias the same font size token. The Number field, the Search field and the Textarea follow through the mirror check (decision field-family-mirrors). Supersedes sizes: the 32 / 40 / 48 px minimum heights, the 8 / 12 / 16 px inline padding, the 0.6 px border, the 4 px corners and the 14 px label, description and error message of that decision are unchanged here; only the text of the large size changes, from 20 to 16 px, and the line height from 1.5 to 1.2.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep today's text (small 14, medium 16, large 20 px, line height 1.5: the large size breaks the rule); B, the Button's whole label style (medium weight, compact line height 1.0, tight letter spacing), rejected because people's content would look like a control label, descenders and accents would touch the line, and the Typography foundation would need an exception; C, the Button's text size with the Typography foundation's single-line style (regular weight, normal letter spacing, tight line height 1.2), chosen; D, the Button's text size with the line height 1.5, rejected because that line height is meant for running text. The Textarea, which holds several lines, takes the same 1.2 line height by team decision (step 3b, option A; rejected: B, its own line height 1.5, the foundation's running-text value), the mirror staying whole.

decisions.text: The Number field, the Search field and the Textarea render the same box as the Text field of the same size and state: height, inline padding, text, border, corners, colors, focus ring, label, description, message and motion are the Text field's, in every platform and mode. A decision on the Text field's box applies to the three in the same change, and pnpm validate fails when a token they share differs (MIRRORS in scripts/lib/mirrors.mjs). What a field has alone is declared, not compared: the Search field's glyph and its start padding, which is a sum (glyph margin + glyph size + the gap before the text) and is recomputed whenever the box's inline padding or the glyph changes; the Textarea's block padding. What a field lacks is declared too: the Search field has no read-only state, no severity and no message. The mirror covers rendering only: a contract decision (keyboard, target size, text size, default) is asked for each of the four. The Select is not mirrored.
decisions.rationale: Nothing tied the three plain fields to the Text field: a decision on its box left them behind. Mirroring them lets every rendering step of the Text field refinement change the four in the same commit, and pnpm validate prove they agree, where the alternatives (the Text field alone, with a closing step per sibling or an issue for the others) leave the siblings out of step in between. The Select is not mirrored now (the team considered mirroring it too, as Figma draws its chevron in the Text field's resting variants): its listbox makes it one of the complex controls, which get their own step once the Text field is settled.

decisions.text: The control shows one of three severities, set by the severity property (none by default, error, warning, success): its border takes the severity's accent functional border color and the message, the message property shown only with a severity, takes the severity's functional text color. A message carries every severity, in the same part; severity replaces the invalid property and message replaces errorMessage. On the web the error is aria-invalid="true" (and :user-invalid when the browser validates) and the severity is also data-severity; warning and success have no web state and are said in the message text. The fill, the icon and the message wording of each severity are rendered in Forms step 6. The accent borders reach 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1); the light warning border is 2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, which step 6 may use as the fill, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).
decisions.rationale: The team validated the Forms foundation's three severities (decision forms-validation-severities) and named the property severity; "error" is the word every platform uses (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, Compose error semantics, Material error text), where "invalid" is the web's technical term. The clean break is deliberate: the packages are alpha and unreleased, and a deprecated alias would cost a schema field and support in the validator, the bridge and the templates. This amends decisions field-colors and label-description-error, whose text still says invalid and error message.

decisions.text: The control is a box on the default surface outlined in the accent neutral border color; hover tints it with the surface hover color and keeps the border; invalid takes the base error border; read-only takes the level 1 surface; disabled takes the shared disabled colors. Value text is primary, the placeholder tertiary, the description secondary, the error message the error text color.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library maps no color to form controls. The accent neutral border is the lightest neutral border that keeps 3:1 against the surface in both modes (WCAG 1.4.11); the hover tint reuses the surface's own hover step.

decisions.text: Three sizes from the Figma library's space and body scales: small (32 px high, 8 px inline padding, 14 px text), medium (40, 12, 16, the default) and large (48, 16, 20); the border is 0.6 px (stroke-width.sm) and the corners 4 px (corner-radius.xs) at every size; label, description and error message keep 14 px.

A field always has a visible label above the control; help text goes under the control as the description, and the error message under it while the field is invalid. Both are exposed as the control's description.

The text field is a single-line text input; the input type (text, email, tel, url) and the autocomplete token are passed as extra attributes of the web template and do not change its look. Search, password and number fields are separate decisions.

changelog.note: Decision fill-page-level: the box keeps the page's level as its fill (text-field.control.background.*: global.bg.level.0.default at rest, .hover on hover, global.bg.level.1.default when read-only), rather than Figma's level 1 or the Button's translucent subtle fill (fails 1.4.3 for the placeholder in dark). Contrast at rest on level 0, light / dark: value 19.03:1 / 11.28:1, placeholder 6.08:1 / 6.40:1 (lowest over levels 0 to 3: 5.75:1 / 5.86:1). Kept as it was: no token or rendering change. The disabled fill is out of this decision.

Decision state-outline-flush: focus is an outline of 2.4 px (focus.ring.width, color.focus.ring) drawn flush over the 0.6 px border, offset minus the border width, instead of a ring 4 px away; a severity (error, warning, success) is an outline of 1.2 px (stroke-width.md) in the severity's border color (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default), 2.4 px in that color with focus; the border and the text never change; outline-offset.focus-visible removed. Contrast, light / dark: focus outline 5.77:1 / 12.76:1 on the default surface (5.45 / 9.58 on level 3); severity outlines as the severity borders, on the default surface and at least on every surface level: error 6.12:1 / 4.97:1 and 5.79 / 3.73, warning 3.27:1 / 8.09:1 and 3.09 / 6.07, success 7.87:1 / 6.08:1 and 7.44 / 4.57. WCAG 2.4.13 is no longer claimed.

Decision radius-button: the corner radius of the box is the Button's at the same size (text-field.control.border-radius per size: small corner-radius.2xs, 2 px; medium and large corner-radius.xs, 4 px; it was corner-radius.xs, 4 px, at every size). Colors, sizes and typography unchanged.

Decision part-gap-6: the parts of the field are 6 px apart at every size and in every state (text-field.container.gap: space.4 to space.6, 4 px to 6 px between the label, the box, the description and the message). The box never moves between states. Colors, sizes and typography unchanged.

Decision label-help-text-sizes: the label scales with the field (14 / 16 / 16 px) and the help text shrinks (12 / 12 / 14 px) (text-field.label.typography: one 14 px style becomes small, medium and large, font size body.size.sm to sm / md / md, line height normal 1.5 to tight 1.2; text-field.description.typography and text-field.message.typography: body.size.sm to xs / xs / sm, so 14 px becomes 12 / 12 / 14 px; weights, normal line height and letter spacing kept). The Size property now affects the label, the description and the message. pnpm validate now fails when the label and the value alias different font size tokens. Colors unchanged; contrast re-measured on levels 0 to 3: description 12.78:1 (levels 0 and 2) and 12.09:1 (levels 1 and 3) in light mode, 8.86:1, 8.11:1, 7.43:1 and 6.65:1 on levels 0 to 3 in dark mode; error text 6.12:1 and 5.79:1 (levels 0 and 2, then 1 and 3) in light mode, 7.06:1, 6.47:1, 5.92:1 and 5.30:1 in dark mode, the same on every platform; 4.5:1 required (WCAG 1.4.3), the lowest being 6.65:1 (description) and 5.30:1 (error text).

Decision padding-inline-button: the inline padding of the box (text-field.control.padding-inline.*, space.8 / 12 / 16) is recorded as the Button's inline padding without an icon at the same size, so a field and a Button start their text at the same inset. Kept as it was: no token or rendering change.

Decision box-height-button: the minimum height of the box takes the height of the Button of the same size (text-field.control.min-height.*: small space.32 to space.28, medium space.40 to space.36, large space.48 to space.44, so 32 / 40 / 48 px become 28 / 36 / 44 px); inline padding unchanged, no block padding. Target size (WCAG 2.5.8): every size stays above 24 x 24 CSS px; the iOS and Android guidelines now say the sizes under the 44 pt hit region and the 48 dp touch target. Colors unchanged, so contrast is unchanged.

Decision value-text-button-size: the value and placeholder text takes the text size of the Button of the same size (small 14, medium 16, large 16 px, body.size.sm / md / md; the large size was 20 px) with regular weight, normal letter spacing and the tight line height (text-field.control.typography.*: large font size body.size.lg to body.size.md, line height normal 1.5 to tight 1.2 at every size). pnpm validate now fails when text-field.control.typography.<size> and button.label.typography.<size> alias different font size tokens. Supersedes sizes. Colors unchanged, so contrast is unchanged (placeholder 6.08:1 light and 6.40:1 dark, value 19.03:1 light and 11.28:1 dark, on the default surface).

Decision field-family-mirrors: the Number field, the Search field and the Textarea are mirrors of the Text field (scripts/lib/mirrors.mjs), so a decision on its box changes the four in one commit and pnpm validate fails when they differ. The Select is not mirrored yet. No token, CSS or template change: the shared tokens already resolve to the same values in every platform and mode, so sizes, colors and contrast are unchanged.

Breaking, decision forms-severity: the invalid property is replaced by severity (none, error, warning, success), errorMessage by message and the part error-message by message, the state invalid by error, warning and success; the web attribute data-invalid by data-severity. Tokens: control.border-color.invalid is control.border-color.error, with warning and success and reads the accent functional border (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default) instead of the base error border; error-message.* is message.*, and message.color.<severity> reads global.text.on-base.functional.<severity>.default. CSS: [data-severity="<severity>"] and [data-state="<severity>"], text-field__error-message is text-field__message. The accent borders reach 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1); the light warning border is 2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, which step 6 may use as the fill, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).

Fix, no decision changed: the Figma library's POC2 export (Color foundation 3.1.0) moves the values of the roles the tokens alias; the tokens, CSS and template are unchanged. Light: 8 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #C01619. Dark: 8 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); control.border-color.default reads global.border.accent.neutral.default: #B9B7B7 becomes #CFCFCF; control.border-color.invalid reads global.border.base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #DF2821; error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #EE5248 becomes #F88275. Contrast re-measured on the accessibility guidelines: 3.82 → 3.73:1, 4.26 → 5.79:1, 4.52 → 6.12:1, 4.97 → 7.06:1, 5.79 → 5.77:1, 6.36 → 6.40:1, 11.27 → 11.28:1, 12.14 → 12.09:1, 12.80 → 12.76:1, 12.87 → 12.78:1, 19.07 → 19.03:1.

Initial draft (decisions field-colors, sizes, label-description-error, single-line-text-only). Native text input in a wrapper with a label element, a description and an error message; states default, hover, focus-visible, invalid, readonly, disabled; sizes small, medium, large. Contrast on the default surface, light / dark: label and value 19.07 / 11.27, description 12.87 / 8.80, placeholder 6.08 / 6.36, error text 4.52 / 4.97 (4.26 on level 1 in light mode), border at rest 12.87 / 8.80 and 12.14 / 8.06 on hover, error border 6.12 / 3.82, focus ring 5.79 / 12.80.
